resources.name: jaildeck API
resources.description:
Jail Deck JSON API collection for Insomnium / Insomnia (export format v4).

Import: Create -> Import -> File -> collections/insomnium.json

NO AUTHENTICATION YET. Mandatory single-operator auth is the Access Control milestone (JD-003); when it lands this collection needs a login request and a session cookie.

ENVIRONMENTS
  FreeBSD guest (SSH tunnel)  http://localhost:8888  jail=ottermq
  Local (fake adapter)        http://localhost:8889  jail=nginx

Jail Deck binds 127.0.0.1 only (JD-002), so reaching a FreeBSD host needs a tunnel:
    ssh -N -L 8888:127.0.0.1:8888 <freebsd-host>

The fake-adapter environment uses a different port so it can run alongside that tunnel:
    JAILDECK_PORT=8889 JAILDECK_ADAPTER=fake ./bin/jaildeck

Adjust `jail` in each environment to a jail that exists there.

RESPONSE QUIRKS
  1. /jails keys are PascalCase (JID, Name, Status, Hostname, IP, Path) because the Jail struct has no json tags; /audit keys are snake_case.
  2. An empty /audit result is `null`, not `[]`.

MAINTAINING THIS FILE
IDs and __export_date are fixed so regenerating does not churn the diff. Re-exporting from the app rewrites both, so prefer editing this file directly.

resources.name: Jails
resources.description: Jail listing and lifecycle. Mutations are logged to the audit trail.

resources.name: Audit
resources.description: Operation history. Append-only JSON-lines file, filtered server-side.

resources.name: Errors & edge cases
resources.description: Deliberately invalid input, to see the real error surface.

resources.name: List jails
resources.description:
Merges `jls` (running) with `/etc/jail.conf` + `/etc/jail.conf.d/*.conf` (configured but stopped), so stopped jails appear too (JD-004). A missing jail.conf means zero jails, not an error.

Response 200: JSON array of jail objects.

NOTE: the Jail struct has no json tags, so keys are Go field names in PascalCase:
`JID`, `Name`, `Status`, `Hostname`, `IP`, `Path`. `Status` is `running` or `stopped`.

This is inconsistent with /audit, which uses snake_case. Worth reconciling before a UI depends on it.

On failure List does NOT go through toAppError, so an adapter error surfaces as 500 `{"error": "internal server error"}` with the detail only in the server log.

Example response:
  [{"JID":"4","Name":"ottermq","Status":"running","Hostname":"ottermq","IP":"","Path":"/usr/local/jails/containers/ottermq"}]

`IP` is empty because that jail uses `ip4 = inherit`, so it shares the host addresses rather than having one of its own. Do not treat an empty IP as an error.

resources.name: Root (redirects to /jails)
resources.description:
Returns 303 See Other with `Location: /jails`.

Insomnium follows redirects according to the global setting, so you will normally see the /jails response. Turn redirect-following off in this request's settings to observe the 303 itself.

resources.name: Start jail
resources.description:
`service jail start <name>` (JD-005). Idempotent: starting an already-running jail succeeds.

Response 200: the single updated jail object (same PascalCase keys as List).

Errors are `{"error": "..."}` with `Content-Type: application/json`.

resources.name: Stop jail
resources.description:
`service jail stop <name>`. Idempotent in the other direction.

Response 200: the single updated jail object.

Errors are `{"error": "..."}` with `Content-Type: application/json`.

resources.name: Restart jail
resources.description:
`service jail restart <name>`.

Response 200: the single updated jail object.

Errors are `{"error": "..."}` with `Content-Type: application/json`.

resources.name: Recent operations
resources.description:
Response 200: JSON array of audit entries, newest first, snake_case keys:
`timestamp`, `operation`, `target`, `command`, `exit_code`, `success`, `error` (omitted when empty).

Default limit 50, maximum 200.

An empty result is the JSON literal `null`, not `[]` — both when nothing matches and when the audit log does not exist yet (it is created on the first mutating operation).

resources.name: Filter by operation + limit
resources.description:
`operation` is lowercased and matched exactly against the logged operation. Any value is accepted — audit records operations from every domain, so it does not keep a list of valid ones. An operation that was never logged simply matches nothing.

`limit`: non-numeric, empty, zero or negative fall back to 50; anything above 200 clamps to 200.

An empty result is the JSON literal `null`, not `[]` — both when nothing matches and when the audit log does not exist yet (it is created on the first mutating operation).

resources.name: Failures only
resources.description:
`success` accepts only the strings `true` or `false`; any other value is ignored and no success filter is applied.

An empty result is the JSON literal `null`, not `[]` — both when nothing matches and when the audit log does not exist yet (it is created on the first mutating operation).

resources.name: Filter by targets
resources.description:
`targets` is comma-separated; entries are trimmed and blanks discarded. A value that is only commas or whitespace means no filter.

Matching is case-sensitive, deliberately: FreeBSD jail names are case-sensitive, so `MyJail` and `myjail` are different jails. Only `operation` is normalised.

An empty result is the JSON literal `null`, not `[]` — both when nothing matches and when the audit log does not exist yet (it is created on the first mutating operation).

resources.name: Unknown jail
resources.description:
Behaviour differs by adapter, which is itself worth knowing:

- `JAILDECK_ADAPTER=freebsd`: 404 `{"error": "jail not found"}` (the only place ErrJailNotFound is raised is freebsd/jail_helper.go).
- `JAILDECK_ADAPTER=fake`: the fake returns a plain error, so toAppError wraps it as 500 `{"error": "failed to start jail \"does-not-exist\": jail \"does-not-exist\" not found"}`.

So 404 is unreachable on the fake adapter.

resources.name: Invalid jail name
resources.description:
Names allow only `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ - .` — anything else is rejected by NewJailName.

Response 400: `{"error": "invalid jail name \"bad name\""}`.

An empty name is also invalid but unreachable through routing, since `/jails//start` matches no route.

resources.name: limit above maximum
resources.description:
Clamps to 200 rather than erroring.

EMPTY RESULT: returns the literal `null`, not `[]`. Confirmed from inside the guest, so it is not a tunnel artifact. The log file is created lazily on the first mutating operation, relative to the process working directory.

resources.name: limit non-numeric
resources.description:
Falls back to the default of 50 rather than erroring.

EMPTY RESULT: returns the literal `null`, not `[]`. Confirmed from inside the guest, so it is not a tunnel artifact. The log file is created lazily on the first mutating operation, relative to the process working directory.

resources.name: Operation is case-insensitive
resources.description:
`START` is lowercased before matching, so it returns entries logged as `start`.

An empty result is the JSON literal `null`, not `[]` — both when nothing matches and when the audit log does not exist yet (it is created on the first mutating operation).

resources.name: Unknown operation matches nothing
resources.description:
Returns `null`, because no logged entry has operation `bogus`.

Before the audit filter was reworked, unknown operations were silently dropped and the request returned the unfiltered list instead.
